description:
Redwood Inference will ship “workload-aware batching defaults”: recommended batching profiles mapped to three customer-facing latency SLO tiers (fast / standard / cost-efficient). The goal is to make batching configuration safer and more automatic—reducing per-token cost for typical workloads while preserving predictable tail latency and avoiding customer foot-guns.

Goals & success criteria:
- Provide tiered default batching profiles (per model family + hardware class where necessary) that meet published latency targets (e.g., p95/p99) while improving throughput and $/1K tokens.
- Make defaults workload-aware: incorporate prompt length distribution, streaming vs non-streaming, and concurrency signals.
- Add observability: per-tier latency/cost metrics, profile selection reason codes, and regression detection.
- Roll out safely: staged launch (internal canary → hosted API subset → Dedicated opt-in → broader default), with clear rollback and per-route overrides.

Scope:
- Runtime scheduler changes (continuous batching heuristics, queue admission/backpressure, max batch size, prefill/decode balancing).
- Config surface area: tier selection at route/model policy level; override knobs for enterprise/Dedicated.
- Benchmarking: representative prompt sets and perf suite updates; publication of recommended profiles.
- Productization: PRD, customer docs, Console surfacing of recommended tier and “why this profile” explanations.

Out of scope (initial release):
- Full auto-tuning per customer tenant in real-time (only recommendations + workload-aware heuristics).
- Cross-region optimization and routing changes beyond existing smart routing policies.

Key stakeholders:
- Serving Runtime (owner): Mateo Alvarez (VP Eng Runtime), Sofia Ivanova (EM Scheduling), Lena Fischer, Marcus Reed, Omar El-Sayed.
- Applied ML / Evals: Jonas Weber, Arjun Desai, Hassan Mirza, Claire Dubois.
- SRE / Observability: Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Allison Grant, Aisha Bello.
- Product: Aditya Rao (Optimize), Nikhil Sharma / Henry Cho (Hosted API), Lauren Bishop (Dedicated) for rollout/override requirements.
- DevEx/Docs: (via docs channels/repos) to update public-facing guidance.

Timeline (hypothetical):
- Discovery & definition (2025-11 → 2026-01): define tiers, targets, benchmark methodology, and candidate profiles.
- Build & integrate (2026-01 → 2026-03): runtime + config plumbing + metrics; initial profiles per top model families.
- Validation & canary (2026-03 → 2026-04): perf canary gates, error-budget checks, regression triage loops.
- Rollout & launch (2026-04 → 2026-05): hosted API gradual enablement; Dedicated opt-in; docs + release notes.

Primary deliverables:
- Confluence design/ADR, tier definitions, benchmark methodology, and rollout playbook.
- Linear plan (eng + PM + design tickets) and linked GitHub PRs.
- Dashboards/alerts spec and implemented metrics.
- Customer-facing docs updates and runtime release notes.

Constraints:
- Must preserve correctness under mixed workloads, avoid starvation, and keep streaming latency stable.
- Must be safe under overload: predictable degradation (backpressure/load shedding) and quick rollback.
- Profiles must be explainable and support enterprise overrides and Dedicated capacity variability.

files.description: Primary design doc: tier definitions → scheduler knobs mapping, workload signals used, selection logic, override hierarchy, and rollout/rollback plan.
ADR capturing the decision to ship three SLO-tier defaults (vs per-tenant tuning), including trade-offs, risks, and mitigations.
Formal SLO tier document: numeric p50/p95/p99 targets, streaming considerations, and how tiers map to routing/policies.
Benchmark methodology for validating each tier: workload mix, prompt-length distributions, concurrency ramps, and pass/fail gates.
How prompt sets are chosen/weighted for tiers (chat vs summarization vs code), including representativeness and known blind spots.
Matrix of recommended quantization variants per tier/model family (where applicable) and compatibility constraints with batching defaults.
Quality guardrails and eval thresholds to ensure batching/quantization changes don’t introduce unacceptable output regressions.
Dashboard/alert spec: per-tier latency histograms, queue depth, batch size distribution, cache hit rate, and regression alerts.
PRD: user stories (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), config UX, default behavior, and launch criteria tied to business goals (cost reduction).
Console design spec: where tier selection appears, recommended tier hints, and ‘why this profile’ explanations for operators.
Plan for updating external docs: tier meanings, how to opt out/override, examples, and FAQ for latency vs cost trade-offs.
Runtime release notes entry describing new tiered defaults, migration notes, metrics added, and known limitations.
Working rollout checklist: canary steps, dashboards to watch, abort criteria, comms templates, and rollback runbook links.
Spreadsheet-style working doc: candidate knob sets per tier (max_batch_tokens, max_wait_ms, prefill/decode split) with benchmark results.
SRE analysis doc: projected error-budget impact, guardrail thresholds, and alert routing during rollout.
Draft metrics taxonomy: naming conventions, tags/labels (tier, model, region), and sampling decisions for high-cardinality signals.
Early PRD draft with open questions, tier naming debate, and requirements for Optimize recommendations vs runtime defaults.
Draft customer-facing messaging: how to explain tiers without over-promising; includes FAQ and examples.
Applied ML experiment log: notes on any quality deltas correlated with batching changes (e.g., truncation edge cases, streaming chunking).
Launch brief: release train timing, dependencies, stakeholders, and external comms readiness checklist.
Notes exploring API surface: request-level vs route-level tier selection, backwards compatibility, and policy evaluation order.
PM ticket to author and socialize the PRD, define launch criteria, and coordinate cross-team dependencies (SRE, runtime, docs).

Implement config schema and validation for tiered defaults; includes migration plan for existing configs.
Add workload signals (prompt length buckets, streaming flag, concurrency) into scheduler decision inputs.
Implement tail-latency protection for fast tier: tighter wait budget, admission control, and starvation prevention.
Tune cost-efficient tier: more aggressive batching, max token batching limits, and safeguards against queue blowups.
